what_it_does: This layer lets forces from different nations, services and agencies exchange operational information (friendly/enemy tracks, orders, geometries, targeting data, intelligence products, logistics status, chat/voice/email) despite owning different C2 systems, different networks, different classification regimes and different national disclosure rules. Technically it spans (1) mission-partner networks and enclaves (CENTRIXS variants, Pegasus for Five Eyes, CFBLNet for lab federation, BICES for NATO/partner intelligence, SIPR-REL / Secret-Releasable, NATO's Federated Mission Networking), (2) cross-domain solutions and guards that move data between security domains under releasability rules, (3) standardized data exchange formats and profiles (STANAG 5525/JC3IEDM and MIP, NFFI, NVG, ADatP-3/USMTF, VMF, Link 16/22, TAK Cursor-on-Target, FMN spiral profiles), (4) federated identity/access (ICAM for partners), and (5) the human/procedural layer (foreign disclosure officers, liaison officers, joining/membership/exit instructions). The recurring failure mode is that information exists in system A on network X at classification Y and cannot legally or technically reach system B on network Z, so people swivel-chair it, re-key it or re-create it at a lower level.

sub_taxonomy.name: Mission-partner network and enclave provisioning (MPE/CIE, CENTRIXS, Pegasus, CFBLNet, SABRE, APAN)
sub_taxonomy.note: Network-centric today; DISA states a shift to a data-centric Coalition Information Environment by early 2027 (FNN, 2026-08-13). Dominated by services integrators (Trace Systems MPE-S, GDIT EMITS 2).

sub_taxonomy.name: Cross-domain transfer and releasability enforcement (CDS, guards, data tagging)
sub_taxonomy.note: Accredited hardware/software guards from Everfox/Forcepoint, Owl Cyber Defense, General Dynamics Mission Systems, Northrop Grumman (CHORD for partner networks). Startup entry requires NCDSMO-class accreditation; evidence of manual product movement persists (SAIC; MIPB 2025).

sub_taxonomy.name: Standards-based C2 data exchange and translation (MIP/JC3IEDM, NFFI, NVG, ADatP-3, VMF, Link 16/22, CoT, FMN spirals)
sub_taxonomy.note: Where allied C2 products compete on 'most interoperable': Systematic SitaWare, HAVELSAN, Terma, ThalesRaytheon AirC2. Annual NATO CWIX is the de facto proving ground; NATO is building INSPECT for continuous conformance testing.

sub_taxonomy.name: Tactical (brigade-and-below) multinational situational awareness bridges
sub_taxonomy.note: Unit-built workarounds (2nd Cavalry Regiment Mission Partner Kit at SBU level) and vendor bridges (Booz Allen Sit(x) connecting Lattice to TAK/partner systems). This is the most accessible sub-layer for a small team because standards are public and data can be unclassified.

sub_taxonomy.name: Coalition intelligence sharing and foreign disclosure workflow (BICES, REL NATO production, FDO review)
sub_taxonomy.note: Evidence shows intelligence produced at collateral Secret cannot be shared and must be regenerated on a lower enclave; BICES does not talk to mission-command systems (MIPB 2025). Institutional and accreditation-bound.

sub_taxonomy.name: Alliance-level C2 programs (NATO ACCS, Maven Smart System NATO, AFSC/airborne C2, LC2IS)
sub_taxonomy.note: Multi-decade NATO programs; ACCS integration 'remains incomplete' after >20 years (Atlantic Council, 2026-06-10). NATO bought Palantir MSS in six months (NCIA, 2025-03-25), showing a faster sole-source path for proven products.

sub_taxonomy.name: Exercise-driven interoperability assurance (CWIX, Bold Quest/JDAT, Talisman Sabre, Steadfast series, Project Convergence)
sub_taxonomy.note: Where pain surfaces publicly. CWIX25: >3,200 participants, ~600 capabilities, >25,000 tests, 40 nations (NATO ACT, June 2025).

users.role: Battle captain / battle manager in a combined joint task force operations center
users.what_they_do: Watches terminals on several networks at different releasability levels, distills information and has staff re-enter it into the system that can accept it (SAIC description of typical coalition scenario, undated ~2022).

Reviews products for release to specific partners; applies most-restrictive-marking rules (NOFORN dominates REL FVEY in combined objects). Human-in-the-loop bottleneck for anything crossing to a partner enclave.

users.what_they_do: Builds and accredits partner enclaves, federates identity, configures guards; DISA says historical practice produced many vertically integrated, domain-specific partner networks now being consolidated (FNN, 2026-08-13).

WADS/PADS controllers integrated with RAAF 3CRU at Talisman Sabre 25 (USAF, 2025-07-28).

Plans reception, staging and sustainment across nations (Steadfast Dart 26: 10,000 troops, 13 nations, Germany as hub). Public evidence insufficient on specific coalition logistics data-exchange tooling failures.

current_architecture.description: Network-centric federation of separately accredited enclaves. U.S. side: CENTRIXS communities of interest per coalition, Pegasus for Five Eyes, CFBLNet for lab/experimentation federation, APAN (unclassified, cloud), SABRE/Secret-Releasable environments, Army SBU MPE, all historically under the Air Force MPE-IS program office and moved to DISA in 2025. NATO side: Federated Mission Networking (spiral specifications) with national systems conformance-tested at CWIX; BICES for intelligence; ACCS for air C2; NCIA-run core services; Maven Smart System NATO for AI-enabled fusion at ACO. Data crosses domains through accredited cross-domain solutions or by humans. DISA's stated direction is a data-centric Coalition Information Environment with zero-trust and attribute-based access, targeted for early 2027 (FNN, 2026-08-13). FACT for the components; INFERENCE for the end-to-end picture, which is not published in one place.

technical_difficulty.summary: The hard part is not parsing formats; most exchange standards (MIP/JC3IEDM, NFFI, NVG, ADatP-3, CoT) are documented and libraries exist. The difficulty is (a) enforcing releasability semantics on structured, aggregated data objects so that they can cross an accredited guard automatically; (b) federating identity and attributes across nations; (c) doing both in DDIL conditions at brigade and below; and (d) passing accreditation for every enclave and guard involved. Link 16 J-series and national fire-control interfaces are export-controlled and closed.
required_expertise: cross-domain solution design and NCDSMO 'Raise the Bar' accreditation
classification and releasability marking (ISM/NTK, REL/NOFORN aggregation rules)
federated identity (SAML/OIDC, ABAC, PKI across nations)
tactical data links and gateways (Link 16/22, VMF)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Automating foreign-disclosure decisions on combined/aggregated data (where the most restrictive marking dominates) in a way accrediting authorities and FDOs will accept; the policy, not the code, is the constraint.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Message parsers/serializers for public STANAGs, TAK servers and plugins, map/COP front ends, chat/email/web core services, cloud hosting at IL5/IL6, PKI.

capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: $3M-$15M (software bridge at SBU/Secret-Releasable); $10M-$30M+ if an accredited cross-domain component is required
capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: two engineers for 6-9 months building a standards bridge (CoT/NFFI/NVG/MIP) with synthetic data. Demo: a government sponsor for CWIX or Bold Quest participation (nations pay their own way), travel, a small integration with one allied C2 product, initial security documentation. Production: ATO/RMF or NATO accreditation, IL5/IL6 hosting, cleared staff, sustainment; CDS accreditation historically takes years and is why incumbents dominate. Ranges are INFERENCE from comparable software-only defense deployments, not from disclosed program costs.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - open standards (JC3IEDM/MIP, NFFI, NVG, CoT/TAK, ADatP-3 elements) and synthetic scenarios allow an unclassified prototype; Link 16 J-series, national fire-control interfaces and real releasability policy cannot be prototyped without government access.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: For anything beyond a demo: exercise data, real marking policy, partner enclave access; MPE/CENTRIXS work is on classified networks.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Link 16/MIL-STD-6016 and many C2 integrations are ITAR-controlled; exporting a bridge to allied customers needs licensing; AUKUS ITAR exemptions cover only UK/Australia. Needs specialist review.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - FMN joining instructions, exercise architectures and most program documents are at least CUI or NATO Restricted.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - the highest-value flows are Secret-Releasable and NATO Secret; a durable product must reach those enclaves.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not for an unclassified/SBU tactical bridge MVP; required for any Secret-Releasable or CDS integration.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person founder (Indonesian national, not a NATO or Five Eyes national) cannot hold a U.S. clearance and could create FOCI and export-control issues for U.S. classified or ITAR-controlled work; a German founder could plausibly participate in NATO/EU work through a European entity (NATO DIANA is open to allied-nation firms) but NATO-classified work is also nationality-gated. The unclassified/SBU tactical bridge sub-segment is the only path that does not immediately collide with these constraints. All of this requires specialist legal review; nothing here is a legal judgment.

why_not_solved.explanation: The binding constraint is national disclosure policy and human FDO review, not software; data produced on national Secret systems without releasability markings cannot legally flow, so it gets regenerated or re-keyed (MIPB 2025; GAO-25-106454).
Every enclave and guard needs its own accreditation; cross-domain accreditation is slow and dominated by a handful of vendors, so new automated paths take years to authorize.

Each coalition, COCOM and service built its own partner network out of necessity (DISA, 2026); NATO capability development has 'delays measured in years' (Atlantic Council, 2025-03-13); nations buy national C2 independently.

No single buyer owns coalition interoperability end to end: DISA owns MPE, Joint Staff owns Bold Quest, NATO ACT owns FMN/CWIX, NCIA buys NATO systems, nations buy national systems, and FDOs own policy.
Dozens of national C2 systems, tactical links, simulation federations and message standards; CWIX ran >25,000 tests across ~600 capabilities in 2025 just to find and fix mismatches.
ACCS (ThalesRaytheon), SitaWare, Lattice and Foundry each aim to be the 'spine'; partner bridges are offered by incumbents (Booz Allen Sit(x) on Menace) which narrows the whitespace.

Data-centric security (attribute-based access, object-level tagging, zero trust) is only now being adopted by DISA (target 2027) and NATO's digital backbone, which is what makes automated releasability plausible at all.
There is no civilian analogue for multinational classified releasability; total addressable spend is program-office services money, which favors integrators over product startups.

For unclassified/SBU tactical SA, government-owned TAK plus commercial cloud (MPK) and vendor bridges (Sit(x)) already work; the residual problem at that level is fielding and training, not invention.

attractiveness.bull: Real, repeatedly documented pain across GAO, Army professional journals, DISA leadership and NATO analysis; DISA's data-centric CIE pivot (2027) and NGC2's data-layer approach create a window where object-level releasability tagging and standards-native bridges become procurable; NATO DIANA and allied sovereign clouds give a European founder a lawful entry path; exercise cadence (CWIX, Bold Quest, PCC, Talisman Sabre) provides visible proving grounds; open standards allow an unclassified MVP.
attractiveness.bear: The binding constraints are policy, accreditation and nationality-gated access, none of which a student-founded startup can change; the paying customers are program offices that buy services from Trace, GDIT, SAIC and Booz Allen; incumbents (Anduril, Palantir, Systematic, Booz Allen) already ship partner bridges; CDS is an accredited oligopoly; a non-NATO-national co-founder blocks U.S. classified and much NATO work; unit-level demand (MPK) has no budget line; SBIR-funded translation tools have not transitioned in ~20 years.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for the segment overall; medium only for a narrow, unclassified/SBU tactical multinational SA bridge or for standards-conformance tooling sold to allied vendors and nations, with a required plan for eventual Secret-Releasable integration through a partner with clearances.

market_stage.rationale: The enterprise network layer is mature and in sustainment (large services IDIQs), while the data-centric layer (CIE, NGC2 data mesh, NATO digital backbone) is mid-transition with prototypes being tested in 2026 and a 2027 target. Tactical multinational bridges remain at unit-prototype stage. This mix is best described as Transitioning rather than Emerging or Mature.

proto_purgatory.notes: Two patterns: (1) data-translation SBIRs (IET Quik-Speak, Securboration C2OSIF, Cougaar BattleFish, Machina Cognita NOVA, RTI) spanning many years with no production transition found; (2) exercise demonstrations (ACIS 2018, MPK 2024-2025, Project Overmatch participation by small vendors with 'no definitive contract awards' per an OPT 10-K) that repeat without programs of record. Counter-evidence: MPE-S, EMITS 2, NGC2 and Maven NATO show that production money flows to integrators and platform incumbents, not to point translation tools.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for translation-tool and 'universal adapter' startups; opportunity only where a product rides an existing production vehicle (NGC2 data layer, DISA CIE task orders, allied C2 vendor partnerships) or a NATO sole-source style buy after proven exercise performance.

candidate_gaps.title: Born-releasable structured data: object-level releasability tagging and automated disclosure decision support for C2/intel objects
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Information created on national-Secret systems lacks machine-enforceable releasability, so it cannot cross to partner enclaves without humans regenerating or re-keying it.
candidate_gaps.user: Multinational intelligence cell analysts, foreign disclosure officers, CJTF battle managers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Product or track is created on SIPR/national system at collateral Secret. 2) Analyst or FDO reviews for release. 3) Product is re-created or sanitized on the MPE/REL enclave (WFX 24-03: switched simulation feed to IEWTPT on the lower enclave). 4) Transfer through an accredited CDS or manual re-entry. 5) Partner ingests via its national system if formats align.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Human FDO review; CDS with static filters; policy of producing at the lowest level; DISA's planned data-centric CIE with zero trust (2027).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Markings are document-level and non-aggregating (NOFORN dominates), so structured/aggregated data cannot be auto-released; every new automated path needs accreditation.

evidence.claim: Officials cited inability to readily share classified information with allies and mission partners
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Collateral-Secret intel precluded sharing; regenerated on MPE lower enclave with REL NATO markings
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DISA moving MPE from network-centric to data-centric by early 2027 with zero trust
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Coalition partners manually move products via CDS; battle managers distill from multiple terminals for re-entry
evidence.label: FACT (workflow) / INFERENCE (prevalence)

evidence.claim: Releasability markings must be applied as most-restrictive across combined objects
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Requires classified access, CDS-class accreditation and FDO policy acceptance; buyers are DISA/COCOM program offices served by integrators; no commercial analogue.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - CDS vendors and Palantir/Anduril can add tagging and policy engines; DISA may build it into CIE.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A tagging/labeling SDK and policy-simulation tool that lets producers see releasability of a structured object at creation time (before it hits a guard), validated against FMN/ISM marking schemas; sell first as unclassified tooling for exercise data preparation.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-standard (JC3IEDM/NVG/CoT) object labeler with configurable REL/NOFORN aggregation rules, audit log and a 'would this pass' simulator; demo with synthetic WFX-style data.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Marking schemas and sample releasable exercise data (CUI); real policy requires government sponsor.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Downstream CDS vendors and DISA CIE; upstream C2/intel producers (SitaWare, DCGS-A successors, Maven).
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: SBIR/STTR (Army, DISA), NATO DIANA challenge, or as subcontractor to a CIE task-order holder.
candidate_gaps.why_now: DISA's 2027 data-centric target and NGC2's data-layer approach make object-level policy a procurement topic for the first time.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: FDO policy remains human-in-the-loop by regulation; accreditation timelines exceed startup runway; non-U.S.-person founder blocks access.

candidate_gaps.title: Brigade-and-below multinational SA/C2 bridge at SBU/Secret-Releasable (productized Mission Partner Kit)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: U.S. and allied tactical units cannot quickly share position, geometry, chat and voice across national C2 systems, so regiments build ad hoc kits and rely on liaison officers.
candidate_gaps.user: Battalion/brigade S3/S6, liaison officers, fires cells, allied battalion staffs
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Allied unit arrives with national BMS (e.g., SitaWare, national FCS). 2) U.S. LNO brings Nett Warrior/MPK or a TAK device. 3) Positions are shared through cloud-hosted COP if connectivity exists; otherwise by voice/radio. 4) Geometries re-entered by hand in each national system. 5) Fires data passed via voice or liaison because C2IS-to-FCS links fail.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: 2CR Mission Partner Kit (SBU, cloud-hosted, COTS); Booz Allen Sit(x) connecting Lattice to TAK/partner systems; ACIS hub; NFFI/NVG feeds where configured.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Kits are unit-built, cloud-dependent, not programs of record, and rely on trained LNOs; C2IS-to-FCS data exchange breaks on geometry discipline and national interfaces.

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: TAK is government-owned and free; Systematic and Anduril/Booz already offer bridges; unit-level buyers have no budget line; repeated urgent-need solutions never became programs of record.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - Sit(x) and SitaWare already market this; NGC2 data layer could absorb it.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A DDIL-tolerant, standards-native (CoT, NFFI, NVG, MIP-lite) edge broker that runs on a laptop/phone without cloud, with geometry validation and an LNO-friendly UI; positioned as the offline counterpart to cloud-hosted MPK.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Edge service bridging ATAK/TAK Server to a SitaWare-compatible NFFI/NVG feed with store-and-forward sync and geometry conformance checks; demonstrate with synthetic data at an allied battle lab or CWIX Innovation Sandbox.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Unclassified: public STANAG samples and synthetic scenarios; later exercise data (CUI).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK, SitaWare, Lattice; radio transport (TSM/other) via IP.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: NATO DIANA or CWIX Innovation Sandbox; Army xTech/SBIR; partnership with an allied C2 vendor; sale to a European MOD first.

candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Government-owned TAK plus MPK is 'good enough'; incumbents bundle bridges free; no program of record emerges.

candidate_gaps.title: Continuous FMN/NATO-standards conformance testing as a service for allied C2 vendors and nations
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Interoperability conformance is verified mostly once a year at CWIX, so defects surface late and vendors lack a year-round harness.
candidate_gaps.user: National C2 program test engineers, allied C2 vendors (HAVELSAN, Terma, Systematic), NATO ACT interoperability staff
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Nation registers capability for CWIX. 2) Tests against other nations' live systems over three weeks in June. 3) Failures logged; fixes deferred to next year. 4) Compliance registry updated per FMN spiral.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: CWIX, TIDE Sprint/Hackathon, NATO's INSPECT platform (near-fielded, aims at 24/7/365 automated conformance).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Annual cadence; INSPECT is government-built and may close the gap itself.

candidate_gaps.killer_risk: INSPECT makes a commercial harness redundant; TAM too small to venture-scale.

saturation_statement: Research is NOT at saturation. 31 searches executed (14 web, 17 Bigdata.com); 36 further queries were attempted but denied because the session's web-search budget (200/200) was exhausted by other agents, the egress proxy blocked every WebFetch/curl host (gov, NATO, news and vendor domains alike), and Bigdata.com ran out of credits.
